text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office maintains sequential intake registers, cross-references applicant identifiers against issued authorizations, and logs every document state change with timestamps to preserve an auditable chain of custody.

2) What occurred: On a dated day, the actor logged into a named ticketing platform account. On a dated day, the actor opened the single valid digital ticket record in a local device file. On a dated day, the actor duplicated the ticket record into multiple copies, each retaining the same ticket identifier field. On a dated day, the actor modified the status field in each copy to a "valid" state. On a dated day, the actor altered the QR code field in each copy to produce identical scannable payloads. On a dated day, the actor listed each copy for sale on a secondary marketplace channel, one listing per document. On a dated day, the actor sent each sold copy to a separate buyer account through a direct messaging channel. On a dated day, the actor instructed the first buyer to present their copy at the venue gate before the remaining buyers. On a dated day, the actor disabled the email notification setting in the ticketing platform account to suppress refund alerts. On a dated day, the actor used a different payment account for each sale to isolate transaction records. On a dated day, the actor removed the device that created the copies from the platform's trusted device list. On a dated day, the actor deleted the local file directory containing the duplicate ticket documents. On a dated day, the actor closed the named ticketing platform account. On a dated day, the actor changed the billing address field on the original account to a different named address. On a dated day, the actor unlinked the payment instrument from the original account.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the named ticketing platform account with a username and password. The actor accessed a local device file system to store and modify ticket documents. The actor accessed a secondary marketplace channel to post sale listings. The actor accessed direct messaging channels to transmit ticket documents to buyer accounts. The actor accessed a payment processor to create separate transaction records. The actor accessed the venue gate scanning system indirectly through the issued QR code payloads.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple sale listings on the secondary marketplace channel shared the same ticket identifier field with different document hashes. The ticket status field in each copy read "valid" while the platform database showed the original as "used" after the first scan. The QR code field across all copies produced identical decoding payloads. Buyer account messages contained identical ticket documents with matching document timestamps. The original platform account showed a billing address change on a date later than the last ticket sale. The trusted device list showed a removal event on a date later than the ticket duplication. The device file system log showed bulk deletion of a directory containing the duplicate documents on a date later than the last sale. Refund alert suppression was enabled in the account settings on a date matching the first buyer transaction.
